name: Greendale
headline: A factory village on West Boylston Street,
with its library and meeting hall side by side.
answer: Greendale is a North Worcester neighborhood along West Boylston Street that grew around the Norton Company's abrasives works, built on the city's outskirts in 1886 and now part of Saint-Gobain. Its civic block on West Boylston Street holds a fire station, a 1913 branch library and the Greendale Village Improvement Society building, put up between 1897 and 1900. WRTA Routes 30 and 31 run on West Boylston Street, and I-190 passes Indian Lake nearby.
meta: Greendale, Worcester: the Norton works, a 1913 branch library and the Village Improvement Society hall on West Boylston Street, with Indian Lake and Shore Park nearby.

boundaries.text: Greendale is in North Worcester, strung along West Boylston Street. Its civic buildings stand together on the east side of West Boylston Street at Kendrick Avenue, the article on the Thomas Giguere Three-Decker, on Fairhaven Road east of West Boylston Street, places it in 'Worcester's northern Greendale neighborhood', and the old Greendale YMCA stood beside Indian Lake where I-190 now runs.

overview: Greendale grew up around a factory. In 1886 the partners of the Norton Company, an abrasives maker, built a new plant on the outskirts of Worcester near two rail lines, in what Wikipedia describes as the Greendale neighborhood, and by 1900 the company employed more than 200 people. Transit followed: the street railway's North End line was extended north to Greendale in the early 1890s. The Greendale Improvement Society, founded in 1895 and rechartered in 1897 as the Greendale Village Improvement Society, built, maintained and plowed roads, lobbied the city for fire protection and arranged trash removal; the Kendrick family gave it land for a meeting house, which was put up between 1897 and 1900 at 480 West Boylston Street.

The city's own buildings came next to it. In 1895 the library set up a book delivery point at a Greendale shop, and in 1913 it opened a branch at 470 West Boylston Street, a single-story brick building with limestone trim, a tile hipped roof and Corinthian pilasters designed by Lucius W. Briggs; renamed for Frances Perkins in 1994, it is still a branch of the Worcester Public Library. The Greendale fire station stands nearby at 438 West Boylston Street. On Fairhaven Road stands a National Register-listed Colonial Revival three-decker of about 1926.

Norton shaped the neighborhood well into the 20th century. Its Greendale YMCA branch, founded in 1929, ran programs at a Norton fieldhouse and had its own building on Stores Street by 1950, on land the company gave; in 1970 discussions began about building Route 52, now I-190, and tearing it down. Norton was bought by Saint-Gobain of France in 1990, and its Worcester site is now part of the Saint-Gobain complex. Indian Lake, once North Pond and dammed in 1828 to feed the Blackstone Canal, lies close by, with a renovated beach and bathhouse at Shore Park on its north end.

housing.text: No published count of housing types or ownership for Greendale alone was found. The National Register lists the Thomas Giguere Three-Decker at 18 Fairhaven Road, a Colonial Revival three-decker of about 1926 with a full-width colonnaded first-floor porch, half-width porches above and a three-car garage. The city notes that the land around Indian Lake has remained primarily residential.

areas.name: West Boylston Street civic block
areas.line: The Greendale fire station at 438, the Frances Perkins Branch Library at 470 (at Kendrick Avenue) and the Greendale Village Improvement Society building at 480, all on West Boylston Street.

areas.name: The Norton works
areas.line: The abrasives plant Norton's partners built on the city's outskirts, now part of the Saint-Gobain complex on the former Norton Company site.

areas.name: Fairhaven Road
areas.line: A street east of West Boylston Street in Greendale, with the National Register-listed Thomas Giguere Three-Decker at number 18.

commute.text: Greendale has no rail station; the nearest is Worcester station at Union Station, 2 Washington Square, downtown, on the MBTA Framingham/Worcester Line. WRTA Route 30 (West Boylston Walmart via Grove and West Boylston Streets) and Route 31 (Lincoln Plaza via Elm and West Boylston Streets) serve West Boylston Street, and I-190 runs beside Indian Lake.

places.name: Frances Perkins Branch Library
places.line: The former Greendale Branch Library, opened in 1913 at 470 West Boylston Street to a design by Lucius W. Briggs, renamed for Frances Perkins in 1994 and listed on the National Register in 1980.

places.name: Greendale Village Improvement Society Building
places.line: The village society's meeting hall at 480 West Boylston Street, put up between 1897 and 1900 on land given by the Kendrick family and listed on the National Register in 1976; it later housed veterans' organizations.

places.name: Shore Park, Indian Lake
places.line: A 7-acre city park on Shore Drive at the north end of Indian Lake, with a large beach, a bathhouse renovated in 2018, picnic areas and a volleyball court.

places.name: Indian Lake
places.line: A 193-acre lake, originally North Pond, dammed in 1828 to supply the Blackstone Canal and later an ice-harvesting site; it is open to boating, swimming and fishing, with personal watercraft prohibited.

places.name: Thomas Giguere Three-Decker
places.line: A Colonial Revival three-decker of about 1926 at 18 Fairhaven Road with a full-width colonnaded porch on the first level and half-width porches above, listed on the National Register in 1990.

history.text: The Norton Company partners built a new abrasives factory on the outskirts of Worcester near two rail lines.
The Greendale Improvement Society was founded to improve conditions in the neighborhood; it was rechartered as the Greendale Village Improvement Society in 1897.
The Greendale Branch Library opened at 470 West Boylston Street.
By this year the Greendale YMCA had its own building on Stores Street, on land given by Norton; the site later gave way, at least in part, to I-190.

Research searches for Greendale returned Wikipedia National Register pages, individual Redfin and MLS listings, and pages about the demolished Greendale Mall; no guide ties the neighborhood's Norton history, its West Boylston Street civic block and Indian Lake together with sources.

faq.q: What is the median home price in Greendale, Worcester?
faq.a: The Warren Group does not report Greendale separately. Citywide, the median single-family sale price in Worcester for calendar year 2025 was $430,000 across 884 sales, up from $420,000 across 904 sales in 2024, according to its MA December 2025 Sales, Prices by Town report.

faq.q: Is there commuter rail near Greendale?
faq.a: Greendale has no station of its own. The nearest is Worcester station at Union Station, 2 Washington Square, downtown, on the MBTA Framingham/Worcester Line. WRTA Routes 30 and 31 run along West Boylston Street.
Worcester Public Schools. School assignment is by address and is set by the district; review the district's profile with DESE.

faq.q: Is there a public beach near Greendale?
faq.a: Yes. Shore Park, a city park on Shore Drive at the north end of Indian Lake, has a large beach and a bathhouse renovated in 2018, and the city's Indian Lake Beach is on the lake's eastern side at 34 Sherburne Avenue.

notes: Written 2026-10-22. No official city boundary for Greendale was found; Wikipedia's neighborhood list places it in North Worcester, and the boundary text is built from the branch library, Improvement Society, Giguere Three-Decker and Greendale YMCA sources. Norton: the 1886 date and 'outskirts of Worcester, near two rail lines' and 'more than 200 people' by 1900 are from referenceforbusiness.com; Wikipedia's Norton Abrasives article places the factory 'in the Greendale neighborhood' and gives 1990 for the Saint-Gobain purchase (referenceforbusiness says Saint-Gobain took over in 1989 and completed the purchase in August 1990). 1 New Bond St is from the referenceforbusiness header; the current Saint-Gobain campus address was not confirmed on a Saint-Gobain page. Streetcar: Wikipedia's Worcester Consolidated Street Railway article says the North End line was extended north to Greendale 'over the following year' after an 1892 extension, so the overview says 'early 1890s'. The Improvement Society building date: Wikipedia's infobox says 1897, its text says erected in 1900; 'about 1900' used. Kendrick Field: the city page gives District 1 but does not name the neighborhood; it is placed in Greendale by its Kendrick family purchase and Brooks Street location, which should be confirmed. The Ezra Rice House article says only 'far northern Worcester' at West Boylston Street and Wilbur Road; its inclusion in Greendale should be confirmed. The Charles Newton House (24 Brattle St, c. 1846) was left out because no source places it in Greendale. Indian Lake: Wikipedia's neighborhood list names 'Indian Lake East' as a separate North Worcester neighborhood, so the lake is presented as a nearby amenity; the 193-acre figure is from the city's Indian Lake Beach page. The Greendale YMCA story is from a 2019 Telegram & Gazette 'Then & Now' piece reposted by the YMCA of Central Massachusetts; the current YMCA branch location was not checked and is not stated. The Greendale Mall (7 Neponset St, opened 1987, demolished 2021) was left out: Wikipedia locates it near the I-290 and I-190 interchange but does not place it in the neighborhood. Market null: the Warren Group PDF lists Worcester only as a citywide row (re-read this session: 'YTD Number of Sales 904 884 -2.2%'; 'YTD Median Sale Price $420,000 $430,000 2.4%'). School assignment is by address and set by the district. Fact-check 2026-10-22: Verified referenceforbusiness (1886 factory on the outskirts near two rail lines; more than 200 employees by 1900; Saint-Gobain takeover reported as 1989 in its introduction and completed August 1990 in its history), Wikipedia's Norton article (factory 'in the Greendale neighborhood which still exists'; Saint-Gobain 1990; the Saint-Gobain complex on the former Norton site), the street-railway article (North End line extended to Greendale over the year after 1892), the Improvement Society article (founded 1895, rechartered 1897, roads, plowing, fire protection, trash; Kendrick land; veterans' organizations after WWII; NRHP November 7, 1976; east side of West Boylston Street between Airlie Street and the library), the branch library article (470 West Boylston Street at Kendrick Avenue; 1913; Lucius W. Briggs; brick, limestone, tile hipped roof, Corinthian pilasters; 1895 delivery point; renamed 1994; NRHP 1980), the city fire stations page (Greendale, 438 West Boylston Street), the library's locations page, the Giguere article, the city's Shore Park (7 acres, 85 Shore Drive, north end of Indian Lake, bathhouse spring 2018) and Indian Lake Beach pages (34 Sherburne Avenue on the east side; 193 acres; North Pond; 1828 dam for the canal; ice harvesting; uses; personal watercraft prohibited; land around the lake 'primarily residential'), the YMCA's 'Then & Now' page and the WRTA routes page. Removed: Kendrick Field (the city's page names no neighborhood, only District 1) and the Ezra Rice House (its article says only 'far northern Worcester'), from places, overview, housing and meta, because no source places either in Greendale. Corrected: the Improvement Society building date (the article gives 1897 in its infobox and text and 'erected in 1900' elsewhere) now reads 'between 1897 and 1900'; the Giguere porch description now matches the article (full-width colonnaded porch on the first level, half-width porches above); the Giguere article says 'Worcester's northern Greendale neighborhood', not 'the northern part' of it, and the boundary and area lines were fixed; the YMCA lines now follow the article ('by 1950'; 1970 'discussions began' about Route 52 and the demolition; the building stood 'at least in part' where I-190 is); the unsourced sentence 'The village organized itself before the city fully reached it' was removed; '1 New Bond Street' was dropped from the Norton area line because it is the company's mailing-address header on referenceforbusiness, not a confirmed plant address.
